deferred_follow_up: Canonical signed-capability integrity has real mutation evidence, but complete stolen-token resistance remains DEFERRED-FOLLOW-UP. The conformance test rejects post-mint scope expansion, untrusted issuer retargeting, and presentation after expiry. It does not bind an otherwise valid stolen bearer token to its legitimate presenter, exercise live revocation propagation, or preserve replay state across restart or failover. Follow-up work must require DPoP or mTLS sender continuity for replay-sensitive grants, qualify durable shared replay state, and add end-to-end revocation tests.
note: Real partial mutation evidence. The conformance test at crates/tooling/chio-conformance/tests/threats/capability_token_theft.rs calls the production floor-aware capability verifier. It rejects a signed token whose scope is widened post-mint with CapabilityError::InvalidSignature, rejects issuer retargeting with CapabilityError::UntrustedIssuer, rejects post-expiry presentation with CapabilityError::Expired, and retains a legitimate-token positive control. A targeted cargo-mutants run forced CapabilityToken::verify_signature_with_floor to return Ok(true); the widened-scope assertion caught the signature-bypass mutant. PARTIAL: otherwise valid bearer-token replay, sender constraint, durable replay state, and live revocation propagation remain deferred.
